highlights: Small modular surgical system with portable bedside units
V-wrist instruments support 360-degree wrist rotation and 3D HD vision
Open console can be used seated or standing

Separate bedside units support flexible laparoscopic port placement. The original FDA review describes a visualization unit and up to three instrument units; portable modularity is not autonomous navigation or autonomous surgery.

The historical UK v15 manual lists an approximately 180 kg console and approximately 100 kg per bedside unit. On printed page 4, console H/W/D is 1325–2085/840/1040 mm and bedside-unit H/W/D 1425/380/380 mm. These are component ratings, not summed complete-system mass or a fixed operating-room footprint, and are not inherited by Plus.

The v15 manual rates at least 20 minutes of bedside-arm battery support, with surgical mode unavailable. The console has no battery and uses mains power; the 20 minutes is not surgical operating endurance or a charge duration.

Original US authorization DEN230078 was granted October 11, 2024 for cholecystectomy in eligible patients 22+. The review describes 11 moving joints per instrument arm and J1–8 for the visualization arm; these are scoped mechanical counts, not an aggregate independent task-DOF rating or clearance for every internationally advertised procedure.

highlights: Plus adds integrated vLimeLite near-infrared fluorescence visualization and a 26-inch 3D HD screen. Overlay/greyscale modes, green/cyan ICG colours and console thumbstick control are described; availability remains subject to local authorization.

The vision offering describes automatic video upload subject to a data-sharing agreement. Software updates and clinical/operational data apps are digital functions, not proof of autonomous surgical decision-making or improved patient outcomes.

The Ultrasonic Dissector is an instrument with a reusable transducer and single-use sterile chassis. Manufacturer claims include vessels up to 5 mm, 250 minutes transducer activation and at most 25 reprocessing cycles; these are not whole-robot runtime, payload or an independent clinical guarantee. The manufacturer explicitly excludes US sale.

FDA K252111 identifies Plus and documents NIR imaging, software and instrument changes relative to original DEN230078. The summary was prepared June 27, 2025 but clearance was December 16, 2025, with adult 22+ cholecystectomy scope at that time.

FDA K261252 records a further Versius Plus decision on October 21, 2026. Exact changes to the indications were not established from the retrieved decision record; the December 2025 cholecystectomy scope is a historical milestone rather than an exhaustive statement of current labeling.

companyFocus.name: CMR Surgical
companyFocus.role: Modular surgeon-controlled minimal-access surgical systems and supporting instruments,vision and digital tools
highlights: The company describes Cambridge UK origins and five founders in 2014. Its portfolio distinguishes original Versius from Versius Plus; manufacturer identity remains CMR Surgical rather than the identities of component suppliers.

Open-console surgical control, separate portable bedside units and flexible port placement define the platform. Plus adds vLimeLite imaging and updated vision/instrument features; imaging tools, instruments, consoles, bedside units and apps are not additional standalone robots.

Availability follows the named configuration, instrument, jurisdiction and decision date. Original 2024 US De Novo, Plus 2025 clearance and a further 2026 FDA decision remain separate. The Ultrasonic Dissector is not approved for US sale; claimed clinical efficiency, software evolution and worldwide adoption are not independent efficacy, universal approval or exclusive superiority.

companyFocus.reviewNotes: Batch 139. Sixteen hashed public responses:15 HTTP 200 and one unused 404; three PDFs with 551 pages of existing text layers, not visual inspection or newly run OCR. Native main/body scope and manual page 32 component-column ownership checked. Three US paths redirect to global homepage and do not verify their requested article/safety content. Exact October 2026 expansion indications from cached search are discovery leads only; FDA K261252 native record verifies device identity and 21 October 2026 SEdecision without detailed label. K252111 December 2025 cholecystectomy scope is a dated milestone, not exhaustive current scope. Original manual component masses/dimensions and 20 minrestricted arm-support battery are not complete-system ratings or transferred to Plus. Instrument joint counts are not aggregate task DOF. vLimeLite, UltrasonicDissector, consoles, bedside units, Trainer and digital apps are components/software, not extra robots. Narrow two-console SecureBoot correction retained in research report, not a universal failure claim. No form, login, contact, message, transaction, patient advice, clinical-outcome guarantee, media reuse, autonomous-surgery or global-approval claim. Portfolio completeness, exclusive superiority and leadership unproven.
